keyVerseText: Jesus said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.
rootMeaning: The word δεῦρο (deûro) is of uncertain etymological origin, but its core meaning centers on the notion of movement toward the speaker's location, essentially 'come here' or 'hither.' This adverb conveys a sense of approaching or coming into presence, often used with verbs of motion or even rest to denote arrival or presence. Beyond the simple English gloss 'come,' δεῦρο carries an immediacy and invitation to draw near, emphasizing proximity and relational engagement.
usageInScripture: Across its nine occurrences, δεῦρο consistently functions as an imperative or adverb expressing the action of coming toward a place or person. Most frequently translated as 'come' (six times) or 'come hither' (twice), it underscores a call to approach, whether physically or metaphorically. This usage highlights both literal movement and an urgent summons, reflecting its role in commands or invitations within Scripture, as noted in Matthew 19:21 and other passages.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, δεῦρο invites believers into a posture of response and closeness to God or Christ, embodying the call to follow, obey, and engage personally with divine instruction. Its imperative force reveals the active nature of faith — not passive reception but a deliberate coming near to Christ and His commands. This word thus encapsulates the dynamic relationship between God and His people, where faith involves movement toward Him, embracing His call with immediacy and trust. Recognizing this enriches our understanding of discipleship as a continual 'coming' into God's presence and purposes.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 19:21, Jesus tells the young man to 'go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.' The use of δεῦρο here conveys more than a mere invitation; it is a compelling summons to draw near and commit fully to discipleship. The word's force highlights the immediacy and personal nature of Jesus' call, urging the hearer to move toward Him in obedience and faith, reinforcing the relational and responsive essence of following Christ.
